nodes.question: What is the most significant portion of greenhouse gases (GHGs) identified in the paragraph?
nodes.answer: Carbon dioxide (CO2) represents the most significant portion of greenhouse gases (GHGs).
nodes.paragraph: The Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change7 has highlighted that activities such as desertification, deforestation, and global warming have environmental implications. The Kyoto Protocol and COP21 are major international climate agreements that address environmental challenges, with participating nations committed to reducing CO2 emissions to diminish global temperature by 2 C13. nodes.question: How have IEAs been perceived in addressing global warming over the past three decades?
nodes.answer: IEAs have been proposed as the only possible solution to control global warming caused by consumption and production activities among all countries.
nodes.paragraph: International agreements offer a platform for integrating national policies into a global framework. Climate change require long-term strategic policy of each country that can be influenced by the obligations undertaken in international agreements. International agreements provide a frame- work for managing conflicts and tensions between countries and promoting policies that not only address immediate needs but are also sustainable and oriented toward a safer future. Agreements, through cooperation among countries, are fundamen- tal tools to ensure that national policies align with global sustainability, inequality reduction, and resilience goals. Studying these dynamics helps to better understand how international negotiations work, the implementation mechanisms, and the impacts of climate policies on a global scale. During the past three decades, IEAs have been proposed as the only possible solution to control global warming, caused by consumption and production activities among all countries. It is common knowl- edge that cooperation in IEAs is quite difficult to reach because each country would prefer to participate in an agreement in order to reduce pollution and preserve the environment but, at the same time, it would pursue its self interest.

nodes.question: What is nitrous oxide (N2O) and why is it significant?
nodes.answer: Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a highly potent greenhouse gas that has a substantial global warming impact and poses a threat to the stratospheric ozone layer.
nodes.paragraph: ORIGINAL PAPERBiology and Fertility of Soils (2025) 61:385 399 https://doi.org/10.1007/s00374-24-1864-3 Introduction Nitrous oxide (N2O) is a highly potent greenhouse gas, exerting a substantial global warming impact and posing a threat to the stratospheric ozone layer (Ravishankara et al. 2009 ; Tian et al. 2020 ). A major contributor accounting for 60% of anthropogenic N2O emissions is agriculture (Sya - kila and Kroeze 2011 ). Denitrification, i.e. the reduction of nitrate (NO3 ) to molecular nitrogen (N2) with N2O as an intermediate, is the major source of N2O. As this process is stimulated under hypoxic to anoxic conditions, the avail - ability of oxygen (O2) is a fundamental physical factor influ - encing N2O production (Groffman et al. 1988 ; Bollmann and Conrad 1998 ; Rohe et al. 2021 ; Schl ter et al. 2024 ). When oxygen in soils becomes limiting, production of N2O via nitrifier denitrification might also account for a high pro - portion of N2O emissions. In this process, ammonia (NH3) is oxidized to Nitrite (NO2 ) which is then stepwise reduced to N2 with NO and N2O as intermediates.

nodes.paragraph: Carbon dioxide removal from triethanolamine solution using living microalgae-loofah biocomposites Tanakit Komkhum1, Teerawat Sema1, Zia Ur Rehman1 & Pichaya In-na1,2 Nowadays, the climate change crisis is an urgent matter in which carbon dioxide (CO2) is a major greenhouse gas contributing to global warming. Amine solvents are commonly used for CO2 capture with high efficiency and absorption rates. However, solvent regeneration consumes an extensive amount of energy. One of alternative approaches is amine regeneration through microalgae. Recently, living biocomposites, intensifying traditional suspended cultivation, have been developed. With this technology, immobilizing microalgae on biocompatible materials with binder outperformed the suspended system in terms of CO2 capture rates. In this study, living microalgae-loofah biocomposites with immobilized Scenedesmus acuminatus TISTR 8457 using 5%v/v acrylic medium were tested to remove CO2 from CO2-rich triethanolamine (TEA) solutions. The test using 1 M TEA at various CO2 loading ratios (0.2, 0.4, 0.6, and 0.8 mol CO2/mol TEA) demonstrated that the biocomposites achieved CO2 removal rates 3 to 5 times higher than the suspended cell system over 28 days, with the highest removal observed at the 1 M with 0.4 mol CO2/mol TEA (4.34 0.20 gCO2/gbiomass).

nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: According to a recent study by Jahanger, which effect is considered the most crucial factor in regulating carbon emissions?
nodes.answer: The composition effect is considered the most crucial factor in regulating carbon emissions, as the impacts of size and technique are deemed insufficient.
nodes.paragraph: In countries with advanced technological innovation and strong institutional frameworks, trade liberalisation positively impacts environmental quality, whereas the challenge of reducing emissions is more significant in less industrialised nations21. Many scholars affirm that the environmental implications of trade openness vary based on the scale, technique, or composite effects8,15,22 More precisely, free trade has a scale effect because an increased trade volume leads to higher production and energy consumption, resulting in elevated CO2 emissions4,23 In addition, the composition effect suggests that trade increases can affect pollution levels, depending on whether a nation S comparative advantage involves trading goods from energy-intensive sectors. According to the technology effect, trade flows among countries enhance competitiveness, efficiency, and the adoption of environmentally friendly technologies in production, thereby reducing environmental degradation. A recent study by Jahanger24 suggested that the composition effect is the most crucial factor in regulating carbon emissions because the impacts of size and technique are insufficient. Shahzad et al.8 demonstrate that the benefits of improved technologies and effective environmental policies outweigh the negative effects of scale and composition on the environment. Depending on which of the three effects is prominent, the overall impact of trade openness on the environment is unclear, although scale and composition impacts are typically dominant in developing countries.
